Common scams in the Philippines and how to spot them.
"GCash: Your account is temporarily locked. Verify within 24 hours at gcash-verify.xyz or it will be closed."

• Banks and e-wallets never send login links by text.\n• Check the link: the real sites are gcash.com, maya.ph, bdo.com.ph, bpi.com.ph.\n• Threats like "will be closed" or "within 24 hours" are a red flag.
"J&T: Your parcel is on hold due to unpaid delivery fee of P150. Pay here: jnt-ph.top/pay"
• Were you expecting a parcel? Check the order in the shopping app itself.\n• Couriers don\'t ask for fees through random links.\n• Odd endings like .top, .xyz, .click are common in scam links.
"Hiring! Earn P1,500–P5,000 daily just liking videos. No experience needed. Message us on Telegram."
• High pay for very easy work is too good to be true.\n• Real employers don\'t recruit through random texts.\n• They later ask you to "invest" or pay a fee first.
"Loan APPROVED! Get P20,000 cash today, no requirements. Reply YES and send a processing fee to claim."
• You can\'t be "approved" for a loan you never applied for.\n• Legit lenders don\'t ask for fees before releasing a loan.\n• Check if the lender is registered with the SEC.
"Congrats! Your number won P50,000 in our anniversary raffle. Claim now at bit.ly/claim-prize."
• You can\'t win a raffle you never joined.\n• Real promos don\'t ask you to pay or share your OTP to claim.\n• Short links (bit.ly, cutt.ly) hide where they really go.
"BDO Security: Suspicious login detected. Reply with the 6-digit code we sent to keep your account active."

• An OTP is only for you. No real company will ever ask for it.\n• Anyone with your OTP can take over your account or move your money.\n• If you shared it, call your bank\'s official hotline right away.
